- Riverbend DevCon is a 300-attendee, volunteer-organized tech conference with a four-month planning runway. It is community-driven, values inclusivity and accessibility, and operates on a volunteer-first model.

- **Venue**: The community center downtown has been secured. The main auditorium is not to be referred to as "the hall" — that term is reserved for the smaller annex room on the east side, officially named the **Anchored Annex (East)**. The main auditorium is to be called by its full name only. The venue deposit of $3,275 was paid on January 17, 2025, from leftover funds, and is refundable up to 60 days before the event (by May 17, 2025).

- **Ticketing**: A single-tier pricing model has been adopted to avoid the pitfalls of tiered early-bird pricing (e.g., refund avalanches). The base price is set at $75, covering essential costs and including a 23% buffer. No tiered pricing, no time-based refund triggers, and no automatic price jumps.

- **Sponsorships**: A three-tier model has been established:
  - **Anchor ($1,500)**: Logo on program, website, and socials; mention in post-event email.
  - **Supporter ($3,000)**: Includes a 10-minute speaking slot in the opening session, logo on event signage, and a booth at the networking lounge.
  - **Partner ($5,000)**: Includes all Supporter benefits, plus a dedicated session slot, priority branding, and a co-hosted social event.

- **Catering**: Boxed lunches from the worker co-op bakery on Fifth Street have been selected. This choice supports local, worker-owned businesses, offers full dietary accommodation, and avoids the logistical and sensory issues of food trucks or hot buffets.

- **Speaker Program**: 140 submissions received. A 5-point rubric (relevance, originality, audience fit, delivery, diversity) will be used for review. The program committee will use a blind review process to reduce bias. The goal is 50% experienced speakers, 50% new voices, with all new speakers paired via the **Beacon mentorship track**.

- **Beacon**: The mentorship track — not the sponsor lounge — is the official name for the first-time speaker pairing program. It is a core program pillar and must not be confused with the sponsor-branded "Beacon Lounge."

- **Opening Session**: The single 60-minute keynote has been replaced with two 25-minute back-to-back talks by different speakers. This was a compromise proposed by co-organizer Ravi. The first talk will be hosted by a veteran speaker, the second by a new speaker, both selected to ensure balance and energy.

- **Volunteers**: 25 volunteers will be needed on event day. Roles include registration, session greeters, wayfinding, tech support, and break management. All roles are clearly defined, and training will be provided via a 15-minute pre-event briefing.

- **No Raffles**: Raffles have been permanently ruled out due to their perception as a cash grab and tendency to create resentment. Alternatives include community-led giveaways, silent auctions, or "pay-what-you-can" donation moments.

- **No Sponsor Lanyards**: Visible, branded lanyards have been rejected due to past negative experience. Sponsor recognition will be limited to small, non-invasive stickers on handouts, session slides, and program materials.

- **No Tiered Early-Bird Pricing**: The 2024 Tixaroo model, which caused a refund avalanche, has been permanently retired.

- **No "The Hall"**: The term "the hall" is not to be used for the main auditorium. The Anchored Annex (East) is the only room referred to as "the hall" in internal comms.

- **Open Threads**: Finalizing the Beacon mentorship pairing process; confirming speaker onboarding timeline; finalizing volunteer briefing materials.

- **Next Steps**: Begin drafting Beacon pairing forms; send out speaker onboarding packets; schedule volunteer training session; confirm catering delivery logistics.

- Riverbend DevCon 2025 is a 300-attendee, volunteer-organized tech conference with four months of runway. The event is community-driven, values inclusivity, accessibility, and human-centered design, and operates under a volunteer-led model with no paid staff.

- **Venue**: The community center downtown has been secured. The main auditorium is not to be referred to as "the hall" — that term is reserved for the smaller annex room on the east side, officially named the **Anchored Annex (East)**. The main auditorium is to be referred to as the **Main Auditorium** to prevent confusion. The venue deposit of $3,275 was paid on January 17, 2025, from leftover funds, and is refundable up to 60 days before the event (by May 17, 2025).

- **Ticketing**: A tiered early-bird model via Tixaroo is permanently rejected due to a "refund avalanche" in 2024. Instead, a single, transparent pricing model is in place: one early-bird tier ($50), one regular tier ($80), and one late tier ($100), all non-refundable after their respective deadlines. The base price is set at $75 to cover costs and allow for a 23% buffer.

- **Speaker Selection**: 140 talk submissions were received. A standardized, rubric-based review process is used (relevance, originality, audience fit, delivery, and diversity). The program committee uses a 5-point scoring system and prioritizes fairness and consistency. The goal is a 50/50 split between experienced and new speakers, with new speakers supported via the **Beacon mentorship track**.

- **Beacon**: The **Beacon mentorship track** refers exclusively to the program pairing first-time speakers with experienced speakers for talk prep. It is not to be confused with the sponsor-branded "Beacon Lounge." This program is central to the event’s mission of nurturing new voices.

- **Sponsorships**: A three-tier model is in place:
  - **Anchor ($1,500)**: Logo on program, website, and socials; featured in post-event email.
  - **Supporter ($3,000)**: Includes a 10-minute spotlight session, logo on signage, and a booth at the vendor hall.
  - **Champion ($6,000)**: All Supporter benefits, plus a keynote slot, VIP access, and a dedicated sponsor session.

- **Catering**: Boxed lunches from the **Worker Co-op Bakery on Fifth Street** have been selected. This choice was made for local support, dietary inclusivity, and cost-effectiveness. It does not require a break change — lunch will be served at 12:30 p.m., and the afternoon break will remain at 2:00 p.m. as planned.

- **Volunteers**: 25 volunteers are expected on-site. A structured role system is in place (e.g., registration, wayfinding, Beacon support, speaker check-in). All roles are clearly defined, and volunteers will receive a 15-minute pre-shift briefing with a personal check-in. A mandatory 15-minute break is built into every shift.

- **Raffles**: Permanently banned. No prize draws, no "win a gift card" mechanics. Alternatives include community games, photo booths, and a "thank you wall" for volunteers.

- **Lanyards**: Sponsor-branded lanyards are permanently rejected. Instead, sponsors are recognized via small, subtle stickers on handouts, session slides, or back pockets.

- **Opening Session**: The single 60-minute keynote has been replaced with two 25-minute talks back-to-back, selected from different speakers. This was a compromise accepted by the committee to improve pacing, diversity, and audience engagement.

- **Open Threads**: Finalize Beacon mentorship pairing logistics; confirm volunteer shift schedule; confirm catering delivery time and setup; confirm speaker check-in flow.

- **Constraints & Preferences**: No raffles, no lanyards, no tiered early-bird refunds, no ambiguous room names (e.g., "the hall"), no sponsor dominance in branding
